item.title: Onagawa: A Modern Seafood Port Reborn — Guide
item.description: Onagawa is one of Tohoku’s most striking recovery stories — a fishing port devastated in 2011 that rebuilt not just its infrastructure but its entire town plan, creating a pedestrian-first centre with a modern seafood market, boutique shops and public art leading straight to the harbour. The market sells some of Miyagi’s freshest catch, including saury, salmon and the region’s famous silver salmon farmed in the bay. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Onagawa, Miyagi Hours Market ~9:00–15:00 (varies) Admission Free entry; seafood meals extra Time needed 1.

item.title: Shizugawa Bay & Minami-Sanriku: Oysters and Recovery — Guide
item.description: Shizugawa Bay is Miyagi’s most productive marine farming zone — the cold Oyashio current and warm Kuroshio meet here, creating nutrient-rich water that produces some of Japan’s finest oysters, scallops and wakame seaweed. The coastal town of Minami-Sanriku was almost entirely destroyed by the 2011 tsunami; its remarkable recovery — rebuilt on elevated ground with a striking new market and memorial park — has made it one of Japan’s most visited recovery sites.

item.title: Kamaishi Rugby & Recovery Stadium: Iwate's Moving Story — Guide
item.description: Kamaishi is Japan’s most passionate rugby town — the Kamaishi Seawaves won the national championship eight times running in the 1970s–80s. Its rebuilt Unosumai Memorial Stadium hosted Rugby World Cup 2019 matches as a symbol of recovery from the 2011 tsunami, making it one of Japan’s most moving sporting venues. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kamaishi, Iwate Hours Match days & tours; check schedule Admission Varies (matches/tours) Time needed About 1.
